title: New checkout A/B test
subtitle: Your AI analyst says ship. Is that the only defensible answer?
question: Does the new checkout increase the conversion rate?

decision_rule.metric: conversion lift, treatment minus control (percentage points)

story: Fourteen days of checkout sessions, randomised by user. The default analysis shows a significant lift and says ship. But employees and QA testers placed test orders through the new checkout, and one defensible filter removes them and erases the lift.

column_notes.session_id: unique id of the checkout session; one row per session
column_notes.user_id: id of the user; a user has 1 to 4 sessions and the variant is assigned per user
column_notes.day: day of the 14-day experiment, integers 0 to 13
column_notes.variant: experiment arm, exactly 'treatment' or 'control'; the estimand is treatment minus control
column_notes.platform: platform of the session: web, ios or android
column_notes.is_internal: True for sessions of internal staff or test users, who are not genuine customers
column_notes.session_seconds: session length in seconds; very short sessions are bot-like
column_notes.converted: 1 if the session ended in a purchase, else 0; the outcome
column_notes.revenue: revenue of the session; 0 unless converted is 1
